subject: Re: Load test coordination & SLO confirmation - Acme Payments
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Load test coordination + SLO follow-up

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the customer-run load test: 

Recap of requirements you shared:
- Latency SLO: P95 inference latency <= 200ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens); P95 <= 500ms for long prompts (~512 tokens)
- Throughput target: sustained 250 req/s for the checkout scoring route (peak bursts to 400 req/s)
- Concurrency: ~80 concurrent connections from your app (we expect keep-alive + streaming for some flows)
- Streaming: you will use server-sent events to stream partial tokens for the payment confirmation flow; expect ~30% of requests to use streaming
- Auth/Accounts: use the provided test API key and test org we created for this run

Ask / next steps:
1) Please confirm the test window you want to run (we suggested Tue 2027-03-30 22:00–23:30 UTC).
2) Send the final k6/Locust script (or confirm we should run yours). We attached a Redwood k6 starter script (acme-k6-script.js) — modify as needed.
3) Provide the source IP ranges for your test runners so we can pre-populate the allowlist.
4) Confirm which endpoints will use streaming vs non-streaming so we can validate socket keep-alive behavior on our side.

Attachments: acme-k6-script.js (k6 scenario with mixture of streaming/non-streaming calls), redwood-test-account-details.pdf (test credentials + rate limits)

I'll stand up an isolated test slice on the Dedicated environment with the configuration we discussed (pinned model version, quantization profile, caching off for initial run). Marissa and Rishi are copied to help with orchestration and to collect metrics.

If that schedule works, we can do a 30-min pre-test sync 30 minutes prior to the window to validate scripts and allowlist.

Thanks —
Logan
Logan Wright
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference\n

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmepayments.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-ops@acmepayments.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Load test coordination + SLO follow-up

Thanks Logan — looks good. A few clarifications from our side:

- Test window: Tue 2027-03-30 22:00–23:00 UTC (we need 1 hour only). Can you confirm availability for that exact hour?
- Scripts: we will use the k6 script you attached but swap in our Locust-based payment flow for streaming tests. I’ll attach the Locust file by EOD.
- IP ranges: our runners are in GCP us-east1. Expected egress ranges: 35.224.0.0/14, 34.96.0.0/14.
- Streaming endpoints: /v1/inference/stream (payment confirmation) will be streaming; /v1/inference/batch (scoring) will be non-streaming.

A couple of ask items:
1) Can you confirm what logging level and RTP headers Redwood will capture during the test (we need request IDs in any logs for correlation)?
2) For the Dedicated slice, what model fallback behavior will you use if we see resource pressure? We want deterministic results for the first run; prefer no fallback.

We'll send the Locust script and a list of lead contact phone numbers for the run shortly.

—Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Payments\n

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Load test coordination + SLO follow-up

Daniel — thanks, all clear. Quick answers inline and plan: 

- Window: Confirmed — we’ll reserve Tue 2027-03-30 22:00–23:00 UTC. I’ll send a calendar invite for the pre-test sync at 21:30 UTC.
- Scripts: please attach your Locust file; our ops team can run it or you can run it from your runners (we prefer you run it to simulate real network egress).
- IP allowlist: we’ll add 35.224.0.0/14 and 34.96.0.0/14 to the test slice allowlist. If you add any additional ranges, send them by EOD tomorrow.
- Endpoints: noted /v1/inference/stream (streaming) and /v1/inference/batch (non-streaming).

Logging and request correlation:
- We will capture request_id, route, model_version, and per-token timings in our test logs. We’ll surface request_id in the response header X-Redwood-Request-Id. We’ll provide a debug log bundle with indices aligned to your request_ids after the run.

Model fallback behavior:
- For this test we will pin the model and disable automatic fallback. No fallback on the Dedicated slice unless you explicitly request it in a follow-up.

Pre-test checklist (action owners):
- Daniel / Acme: share Locust script + list of IPs (action: Daniel) — due EOD 2027-03-29
- Redwood (Logan): create Dedicated test slice + add allowlist (done by 2027-03-30 18:00 UTC)
- Redwood (Marissa): run a smoke test against endpoints at 21:40 UTC before the sync (owner: marissa.cole@redwood.com)
- Redwood (Rishi): enable request_id header and debug logging for the slice (owner: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com)

I’ve attached the starter k6 script and the test account PDF again. Let us know when you upload the Locust file.

Thanks —
Logan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Load test coordination + SLO follow-up

Quick confirmation: I scheduled the pre-test sync 2027-03-30 21:30 UTC (30min) and added the 22:00–23:00 UTC test block. I’ll run the smoke test at 21:40 UTC and post the smoke results in the calendar thread.

If Daniel uploads the Locust file before EOD, I’ll also run a quick parser to validate the scenario rates against our capacity plan.

Looking forward —
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
